ratings.comment: Professor Betsy was a great professor. She would go over the homework on Tuesday so we get more prepared for the weekly quiz. Exams weren't too bad. So if you pay attention in class and sometimes read the textbook for clarification, you should be fine. By the way this review is for Math 475, I don't know why it is not included in the course code.
Elegant explanation of the most intricate concepts.
Not an easy class by all accounts, but she does a great job guiding you through it and seems to genuinely care about you and actually wants you to learn and grasp the concepts
I thought she was a fantastic professor. She explained the concepts clearly and would always be open to answering any questions. I also found her funny and engaging.

Very ineligible writing, go over the material at a way too fast pace so be prepared to take photos of lecture notes with your phone throughout class, would write down a whole chunk of notes before noticing that they have nothing to do with the content materials and then delete them all, lecture contents are too sophisticated compared to exams.

Professor Betsy is generous. Her lecture work is proof heavy, there can be questions in exam which you have never thought of. Be ready to read more and more to develop better understanding. She is accessible outside class and office hours are helpful.

Betsy Stovall is by far my favorite professor I've had at Madison so far. She is incredibly sweet and understanding, and I loved the format of her online class. Her lectures were clear and had plenty of examples, and her office hours were incredibly useful. The exams were easier than the homework, so if you do well on that you'll do well on tests!

Nice person, but not great at teaching. Would ramble on for the entire 50 min lecture about 2 problems and took forever to answer simple questions. Had tons of online videos as the lectures for each section which dragged on and were nothing like the homework or tests. Had to teach myself most of the class, but thankfully it wasn't too difficult.

I had Betsy for Calc 3 during COVID. She was understanding, willing to be flexible, and more interested in us learning the material than in being a hardass with grades. I learned a ton, and since she posted her lectures online in advance, she was able to use the scheduled class time for questions and examples. Ill be looking for her again!

Betsy is a passionate math professor who genuinely cares about her students and the topic about which she is teaching. As someone who took AP Calculus AB prior to taking Betsy's class, I found it easy, however, I still had to study. Great class and great professor!

Stovall is really not a good lecturer. She spends way too much time on proofs and theoretical things that aren't useful. The class is curved which helps a lot. I found her tests to be difficult, but discussion with my TA was very helpful as all we did was practice problems. The practice exams are extremely helpful in studying for tests.

Took Stovall for 234, the material wasn't too bad but her lectures were very theoretical and therefore I did not gain much from her. Her homework and tests were doable, and there was a strong curve at the end. I got C's on the first two midterms and an AB on the final and got a B in the class.

If you're looking for some concrete examples this is not the professor for you. If you really like to listen to endless proofs for over an hour twice a week and can learn from that, go for it. As someone who needs concrete examples to learn, I hated this class and wouldn't recommend Betsy in the slightest unless she's your only option.

Stovall was a very fair and easy to understand professor. Quizzes (10%), homework (5%) (graded on completion), two midterms (25% each) and final (35%). Overall the class was straight forward and exam questions could be predicted based on lecture emphasis. Usually one theoretical question per test, but understanding her various proofs really helped.

She writes more than is necessary for notes so listen more than writing. She is clear in her explanations, but often goes very theoretical and can be dry. Homework is nearly impossible so make use of MathLab and TA hours. Still the best option for 234
The material was extremely tough, but she did a very good job of delivering it.

Lectures were very easy compared to the homework assigned and the quizzes given. Asked theoretical questions and to do proofs on the exams we did not derive in class. Overall I think she isn't very organized with the lecture notes and would not recommend.

Betsy is one of the best harmonic analysts in the country, and I would highly recommend her graduate class. Homework and exams are rather difficult, but she is well aware of that, so the grading is generous and forgiving.

Example oriented and logical. Doesn't use overly advanced language when explaining concepts but doesn't always have time to explain things as slowly as I wanted. She comes prepared for class and tries to keep things as upbeat as calc 3 can be. Exams were hard but fair. Class average was 39/50 on first exam, 29.6/46 second exam.

521 is rough, and she doesn't take it easy on you, but she makes sure you learn your stuff. If you put in the effort and are willing to ask questions you will be an analysis superstar. The lectures are very fast paced, re-reading your notes and working through slowly will yield the best results.

Hard grader--yes. Tough class--yes. Worth it--absolutely! She is very clear in her expectations (she is passionate about rigor), and if you come to class and office hours, it is manageable. I would recommend her!
Professor Stovall is terrific. She explains difficult concepts well and even throws in a little humor. Grading is tough, but that is to be expected in such a difficult course. The curve is generous.

Prof. Stovall does a great job explaining abstract concepts conceptually, as long as you ask her if you are confused.  Sometimes it might be easy to just write things down and read later, but ask while you can so that you aren't struggling later.  Tests are extremely tough, but fair, and HW the same.  Study the proofs and HW and you'll do fine.

Dense lectures with very little explanations as to why methods/operations were chosen. There is almost zero interaction with students during lecture. You will spend the entire period copying writing on the board that has not been explained well, and then be expected to have it memorized verbatim. Tough grader. Teaching is not one of her strengths.
not sure if her name is lindsay or betsy but she's amazing anyways

Alright, ignore all good reviews for math 217 for this woman. She's bad. Doesn't explain a thing, just writes equations on the board then repeats what the equations say. Tests are a pain because she doesn't explain ANYTHING and goes on to give hard problems. 010, and you get to feel super unprepared for a cumulative final. Thanks Khan Academy.

Prof Stovall is extremely nice and cares about the success of her students. That being said, she is so knowledgeable about math that she struggles to explain things in an easy and straightforward way to students -- she assumes that we knowunderstand more than we do. Tests are very hard. Take 211 over the 171217 sequence.

Professor Stovall is one of the nicest professors I have ever had so far. She tries to explain everything clearly, and if she doesn't she will try her best to do so. The first exam was hard, but its because she never taught a lower math level class. Her second exam was fair and nice. Some people hate her, but its because they do not practice...
Worst math class I have ever taken. Do not take her if not necessary.

Betsy's a great professor. She delivers the material in a way for students to understand and she will go over more examples as needed. That being said, Tests are tough. If you do the practice exam a few times to prepare you will be fine. Overall Betsy expresses care for her students and is a great math professor!

Prof Stovall is probably one of the nicest professors that I've ever had, and she genuinely cares about her students and is very accessible. That being said, this class is insanely hard. The average on the first midterm was a 37%. She lectures well, but exam material is crazy hard and combines many topics into a complicated and frustrating mess.
Tests are one hundred times harder than quizzes and homework. Her teaching style is confusing and there are much easier methods she does not teach
Do not take her if you do not have to. She just rambles on up front and does not seem to care that the average for her first exam was 29%. Her tests are very hard.
Easily the hardest exams I've ever taken. Luckily, there was a massive scale, 31 was an A. Lectures are long and very proof-oriented.
Great professor. She really cares about students. The HWs are not easy, but I learned a lot from doing them. And she's very nice and helpful!
The course is hard, but she is really helpful.
She's class. One of the best in the Math Department

Betsy is a terrific professor and manages to simplify real analysis to the point where it is not even difficult. She has a really really really generous curve for grading, and she is really organized in her lectures. The exams are pretty easy and you only need 66% for an A on those.

This class is the hardest undergrad math class you'll take at UW. It's a beast. But Besty is a great teacher. She's really kind and clear in her instruction. Wish I could take another class with her! She's your best bet for sure!!
I really like Betsy. If you have to take real analysis, she's your best best. Very pleasant and knowledgable.
Really helpful during office hours. Make sure you attend them. Homeworks are hard and tests are based on lecture notes. If you take her notes and put in the time( ALOT of it) you should be fine.

What I found lacking was the ability to step out of the realm of mathematics and give examples/explanations that a beginner could understand. While proving theorems, the big picture would get lost when treating the proof just as a set of Mathematical statements without picturing what exactly it is that we are trying to prove. The pacing also lacked

Take this professor.  I went on the waiting list, and I'm glad I did.  This is a HARD class if not explained properly, and she does a great job.  If you have to go on the waiting list to get her for 521, DO IT.  The homework and tests are fair. Now she's a fairly tough grader, but that's a small price to pay.  Great teacher.

It was very hard to learn with professor Stovall, and I often got nothing out her lectures. she never used examples, only proofs to explain things. Maybe her teaching style is for some, but if you like exaples and extra time to learn things, dont take her. Also, very hard tests

She writes challenging exams but her grading scale more than compensates for this. Her lectures were fascinating. Her method of presentation was to write a proof while leading the students through it. At crucial points she would stop and make sure we were still with her. Do the assigned readings, start the homework early, and you will do well.

This class is frustrating. The material is pretty easy, but her tests (very proof based) are hard (49% av on midterm 2). 340 is not suppose to be proof based, 341 is... so not sure why it is. Her lectures are SO boring (almost completely proof based). She is a nice person and means well, but she's just pretty bad... take another teacher if you can.
